clue.text: Group of revolutionary old soldiers

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the little word of is read backwards

parts.note: soldiers are fighters

explanation.surface: A description of a band of veteran insurgents who once overthrew a government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like it describes the soldiers but it turns 'of' round to give FO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Foo Fighters are an American rock band, and a band is a musical group.

clue.text: Person leaving one fellow stuck up hazardous construction

indicators.note: in a down clue, sticking something up means writing it from bottom to top, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a person who leaves or departs is a parter
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone walks out, leaving a colleague trapped high up in a dangerous building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck up' reads as stranded aloft, but in a down answer it signals writing PARTER, I and F upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A building with poor escape routes or flammable materials is dangerous in a blaze, a hazardous structure.

clue.text: Engine starts to overheat dangerously when modified with a turbo

indicators.note: modified means altered, so these letters are rearranged
the starts of the words overheat and dangerously are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A warning that an engine fitted with a turbocharger begins to run dangerously hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' shuffles O and D (the 'starts to' overheat and dangerously) together with A TURBO.
explanation.definitionFit: An outboard is a motor fixed to the stern of a small boat, a type of engine.

clue.text: Institute found in Italy and maybe another country

indicators.note: something found in another is placed inside it

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise, so these three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An institution located in Italy and possibly in some other nation too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges AND to NDA after I for Italy; 'found in' puts the second I, for Institute, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation in South Asia, so it fits as a further country besides Italy.

clue.text: A man prepares leaves for a book

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
making tea from tea leaves is brewing it

explanation.surface: A man readies some pages for a volume he is putting together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' suggests pages of a book, but here they are tea leaves being brewed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to the Hebrews is one of the books of the New Testament.

clue.text: Green vines winding round the tops of oaks, unusually

indicators.note: something going round another surrounds it
winding means twisting, so these letters are rearranged
the tops of words in a down clue are their first letters

explanation.surface: Climbing plants twine strangely round the upper branches of oak trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges VINES to ENVIS, and 'round' puts it around O and U from the tops of oaks and unusually.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is a colour long linked with jealousy, as in the green-eyed monster.

clue.text: With a clear plan of attack, tiger cats scattered

definitions.text: With a clear plan of attack

indicators.note: scattered means dispersed in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Big cats such as tigers fan out as they close in on their prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategic describes action following a deliberate overall scheme, like a planned military campaign.

clue.text: Provide a piece cut from irregular material

indicators.note: a piece cut from the words is a run of letters lying within them

explanation.surface: An instruction to supply a scrap trimmed from uneven cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm someone is to equip or furnish them, especially with weapons.

clue.text: Fish finally gutted and put in a corner

parts.note: to fish with a rod and line is to angle

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of gutted

explanation.surface: A fish is cleaned at last and set aside in a corner of the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set in a corner sits where two walls meet at an angle, so it is angled.

clue.text: What do you call a guy who sprays plants?

definitions.text: What do you call a guy
definitions.meaning: the polite form of address for a man, as in Mr
a device or person that sprays a fine mist over plants

explanation.surface: It sounds like the setup to a joke about a gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: Mister is the title for a man, and a mister is also a fine-spray bottle for houseplants.

clue.text: Blathered on — not quietly — and gave a critical opinion

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for quietly is dropped

parts.note: to prate is to talk on foolishly
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A critic who rambled on loudly before delivering a verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to assess or judge its quality, giving an evaluation.

clue.text: Drinks made in barrels always taking a long time

indicators.note: taking means holding or containing, so the barrels go around the other pieces

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for barrel, so BS is barrels
always means ever
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Drinks that are produced in casks and take ages to mature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made in' only links; 'taking' is the containment signal, the barrels holding the other pieces. B is a recognised abbreviation for barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water, so the plural matches drinks.

clue.text: Art deco building right by the eastern edge of Soho — tourists were entertained there

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are put together afresh
in an across clue the eastern edge of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A description of an Art Deco building on the edge of Soho where visitors were amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun about the Art Deco structure, but it rearranges ART DECO. The London Trocadero was an entertainment centre near Piccadilly Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Trocadero housed attractions and amusements aimed at visitors, so it is a place of tourist entertainment.

clue.text: Subject's art ultimately removed from far side of NY museum

definitions.note: subject is, the apostrophe s standing for is as a link

indicators.note: the letter is taken off the far end of the museum name

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of art

explanation.surface: A subject's artwork has been taken down from the far wing of a New York gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives the T of art, which comes off the end of THE MET, the Metropolitan Museum's nickname; the 's of Subject's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject matter of a talk or work.

clue.text: Appointed region from the east supplies gas

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: an appointed time is a set time
a region is an area

explanation.surface: A designated district from the eastern side supplies gas.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate something is to charge it with air or another gas, as with fizzy drinks.

clue.text: Criminal once hurt with butt of iron club

indicators.note: criminal suggests wrongdoing or something crooked, so these letters are rearranged
the butt of a word is its end, its last letter

explanation.surface: An offender once hit someone using the end of an iron bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short thick stick carried by police, a type of cudgel.

clue.text: Yarn that stretches? It might, say, in the middle

parts.note: it might sag in the middle, as a rope or mattress does

indicators.note: points to the middle letter of the word say

explanation.surface: A question about a thread that stretches, which may droop in the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' does double duty: it completes 'It might sag in the middle' and takes the middle letter of 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, so it is a tale that goes on and on.

clue.text: Mostly well-mannered, endlessly nice and ordinary government minister, perhaps

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: well-mannered means polite

indicators.note: endlessly means without its two ends, leaving the middle letters

explanation.surface: A government minister described as mostly polite, nice and ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is a politician, and a minister in government is one example.

clue.text: Guests oddly dying to take off

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters are kept

parts.note: something dying is going, on its way out

explanation.surface: Visitors strangely desperate to get away from a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To get going is to leave or set off, the same idea as to depart.

clue.text: Cry over an onion?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to blub is to cry or weep

explanation.surface: Someone weeping over chopping an onion.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is an example of a plant bulb, hence the question mark.

clue.text: German inventor, foremost in oils and in command of resin

parts.note: Karl Benz was the German who built the first practical motor car

indicators.note: foremost in means the first letter of the word

parts.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge, in command

explanation.surface: A German inventor, a leader in oils, takes charge of some resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Benzoic acid is obtained from benzoin, a resin from trees, so the adjective relates to that gum.

clue.text: Almost imbibe wine — it's sweet!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to suck is to draw in liquid, to imbibe
rosé is a pink wine

explanation.surface: A drinker nearly gulps down wine and finds it delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucrose is cane or beet sugar, the most familiar sweet substance.

clue.text: Believable story involving a new dog

indicators.note: involving means including, so the story goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a spiel is a glib persuasive story meant to be believed

explanation.surface: A plausible tale that features a new dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of dog with long drooping ears.

clue.text: Dress down in a pile on the floor?

definitions.meaning: to reprimand someone, as a boss might haul an employee over the coals
a floor covering with a pile, its raised surface of fibres

explanation.surface: Taking off clothes and leaving them heaped on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for to scold, and a carpet is a piled rug covering a floor.

clue.text: Main item of office equipment

definitions.meaning: a ... is a principal or basic item, such as a ... food
a small wire clip driven by an office ...

explanation.surface: Something described as the chief piece of office kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is both a basic commodity and the bent wire fastener used to bind papers.

clue.text: Lorry about to leave snowy area

indicators.note: the letter for about leaves, being dropped from the word

parts.note: the Arctic is the snowy polar region
C is the abbreviation for circa, about

explanation.surface: A truck is about to depart from a snow-covered region.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is the British short name for an articulated lorry, a tractor unit pulling a trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulated truck, abbreviated, is a large goods vehicle in Britain.

clue.text: Northern person abandoning Hull in the end? It almost happens!

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: an earthling is an inhabitant of Earth, a person

indicators.note: in the end points to the last letter of Hull

explanation.surface: A northerner finally leaves Hull, a city in Yorkshire, and it nearly comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops L, the end of Hull, from EARTHLING; Hull is a port city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape or close call is an event that very nearly comes about.

clue.text: Vehicles controlled with computers from the rear

indicators.note: reading from the rear means back to front, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: smart devices are computer controlled, as in smart meters

explanation.surface: Vehicles operated by computers located at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are streetcars running on rails, a type of public transport vehicle.

clue.text: Spicy sausages go with Italian lager

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, pep
Peroni is an Italian beer brand

explanation.surface: Hot sausages go well with a bottle of Italian beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-American salami, often sliced on pizza.

clue.text: Politician taken in by excellent excuse

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the politician goes within

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
a Lib is a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A politician is fooled by a superb excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as a defence or pretext.

clue.text: Support is there from time to time

indicators.note: from time to time means now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Help is available only occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf tee is the small peg that holds up the ball before driving.

clue.text: Cool singer and a smashing director

indicators.note: smashing means breaking up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trendy vocalist and a brilliant film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' looks like praise for the director but rearranges COOL SINGER plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolas Roeg was a British film-maker known for Don't Look Now and Walkabout.
